references.text: The same procedure of burning the fat on the altar and obtaining forgiveness is repeated for the sin offering from an ordinary person
Parallel description of burning the fat as a peace offering, where the priest makes atonement so that the sin is forgiven
Describes the fat from the peace offering (זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים) that must be burned on the altar
The priest makes atonement for the person's sin, and they receive forgiveness - the same formula for atonement and forgiveness
The priest makes atonement (וְכִפֶּר) and the person receives forgiveness (וְנִסְלַח) - identical wording
The priest makes atonement for the person before the Lord, and it is forgiven
The fat from the peace offering must be burned on the altar by the priest
The priest makes atonement for the sin, and the person receives forgiveness - the same atonement formula
Mentions that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
The promise of forgiveness for sins when we confess - fulfillment of the purpose of atonement in the New Testament
